parameter_arithmetic_probe.limits: DirectEntry includes generic ABI checks and execution preparation; RuntimeDispatch also converts the result. CppChecked uses exact i128 reduction and final i64 overflow validation, without execution context, global state, exception envelopes or source traces.

measurement_limits: Same macOS arm64 host, pinned toolchain, Release configuration, workload inputs and randomized 7-repetition 0.2s suite; runs occurred in separate processes.
Background load and per-case CV limit small regression or speedup claims. Machine-code analysis independently confirms the reduction remains loop-free and its Ready success path has no runtime calls.

AOT/C++ measures the complete workload including native dispatch, execution state, global access and result handling. C++ arithmetic uses unchecked integers; this is not a per-operation language overhead ratio.

The parameter probe excludes global access and the main suite result wrapper. Its C++ checked kernel retains exact i128 arithmetic and final overflow validation, but omits runtime execution state and exception envelopes.
First-native excludes instantiation. RSS is a resident snapshot of the combined process. Frame/root counters describe planning before LLVM optimization.
Execution was verified on macOS arm64; Windows/Linux and clean-host distribution acceptance were not repeated.

comparison_to_previous.basis: Same machine, toolchain, Release configuration, 28 cases and measurement settings; per-case variation retained.

suite.name: dasProfile complete 16-workload local port
suite.upstream_correctness_limit: Original assertions and exit statuses were checked; some upstream programs have no strong checksum assertion.
notes: All 16 upstream workloads retain the original kernel sizes. Vela is a port of the upstream C++ algorithm; compilation, setup and instance creation are excluded.
cpp_matched and Vela use binary64 for the floating workloads. Original C++ and DAS generally use binary32 except spectral norm. Results across those groups are not numerically equivalent.
Vela int is checked int64. SHA256 and iterative Fibonacci explicitly implement uint32 wrap. The matched C++ uses native uint32 for those wrapping kernels; Vela masks its int64 values.
string2float uses identical binary64 input values and shortest round-trip strings in the matched group; its C++ parser is from_chars. Original C++ uses atof on binary32 values.
float2string in the matched group uses shortest round-trip to_chars formatting. Original C++ uses printf %f; its output length and amount of work differ.
particles keeps state across iterations, as upstream does; the matched group validates the final position against the number of calls. binary64 positions avoid the upstream binary32 saturation issue.

n-bodies in the matched group resets the five bodies per kernel and validates final energy. Upstream C++ and DAS retain state, and the DAS implementation also rescales and vectorizes the update, so its timing is contextual.

tree in the matched group uses the same deterministic priority LCG and split/merge operation stream. Original C++ uses rand and DAS uses random_big_int. Native deletion and Vela GC remain their normal lifetime mechanisms.
sort copies 100000 identical signed int32 noise keys into int64 elements in the matched group, sorts descending and validates order and sum. Original C++ and DAS use int32 elements.
interop makes 1000000 calls to a separate translation unit without LTO. Vela and matched C++ use int64; original C++ and DAS use int32.

Vela uses managed object references, checked arrays, normal host math bindings and GC. C++ uses native structs, arrays and standard containers; storage layouts and safety costs are not made equivalent.

Google Benchmark measures the matched group with random interleaving. The original programs use their unchanged 0.5 second calibration harness, in separate processes. Process startup and compilation are not included in either reported kernel time.
The machine experienced scheduling variation: both wall and CPU medians plus variation are retained for the matched group. Results around 1x should be read as parity, not a demonstrated win.

DAS interpreter and JIT run original .das kernels with external-runtime launch flags disabled in config.das. The official SDK builds the unchanged testProfile binding for host interop. JIT cache is warmed once per kernel.
This experiment did not optimize or change Vela production compiler/runtime code. Existing uncommitted compiler/runtime optimization changes were preserved. No lint was run.
